source.title: Maximum Median Sum of Subsequences of Size 3

teaching.hint: What other values must accompany each of the largest medians you hope to obtain?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: The jth largest median needs 2j distinct input elements at least as large; its value is therefore at most the 2jth largest input.
solution_outline.approach: Sort the values. Reserve the bottom third as group minima; pair the remaining values from largest downward, using the smaller of each pair as a median. Sum those medians.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: Each chosen median has its own larger partner and one unused bottom-third minimum; every group consumes three distinct elements.
solution_outline.correctness: For any grouping, the top j medians and their group maxima occupy 2j distinct values, proving the jth median cannot exceed the 2jth largest input. The proposed groups use those exact even-ranked descending values as medians, with minima no larger than them. They attain every bound simultaneously, so their sum is globally maximal.
solution_outline.complexity: O(n log n) time and O(log n) auxiliary sorting stack space for an in-place comparison sort.
solution_outline.pitfall: Taking the largest n/3 elements as medians ignores the distinct larger partner each median needs.

common_wrong_turns: Taking the largest n/3 elements as medians ignores the distinct larger partner each median needs.
source_fidelity_notes: Preserved arbitrary element selection, multiplicities, complete removal into triples, and wide total; omitted the grouping examples.
